correctness.rationale: The proof writes every complex degree-two spherical harmonic as a trace-free symmetric quadratic, gives all four orthogonal O(m)×O(m) sectors and multiplicities summing to 2m²+m−1, calculates each output/input Gram ratio from normalized second and fourth moments, and treats scalar beta variance. Positivity gives injectivity precisely off t=1/2. On t in (0,1/2), min{λX,λZ} crosses only at the claimed t_minus; normalized spectral ratios are strictly decreasing before and increasing after it, and at that crossing λY dominates λM for m>=2. Symmetry gives exactly two global optimizers. The exact-rational stand-alone cubature code reconstructs all Gram entries on m=2,3,4 and verifies 4779 assertions; finite tests supplement, not replace, the all-dimensional proof.

originality.rationale: The claim combines four explicit full-space trace eigenvalues with sharp global conditioning, two and only two minimizing radii, a coincident E-optimal lower bound, and strict dimension dependence for all m>=2. Search comparison found no matching or dominating statement among the retrieved published results. Zandieh et al. prove randomized whole-sphere approximate recovery; Bangun et al. study finite sensing-matrix coherence. Their quantifiers, sample geometry, and objectives differ. General sphere moment formulas are ingredients and do not themselves specify the sharp Clifford restriction optimizer. The search does not guarantee historic novelty, and an implicit isoparametric branching theorem remains a risk.

value.rationale: Generalized Clifford hypersurfaces are natural homogeneous level sets; stable recovery of the full first even spherical-harmonic band from one hypersurface is an intrinsic sampling problem. A complete dimension-uniform four-sector spectrum yields the exact blind mode, the two uniquely best radii for BOTH minimax conditioning and largest lower frame bound, and the nontrivial asymptotic 1+2/sqrt(m+2). This is not merely a small parameter variant of the cited finite and random sampling analyses; restrictions and normalization are explicit.
